programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: An deis meadhan geama, tha an dèideag aig Sula a’ dol an sàs ann an craobh. Gus cobhair a dhèanamh oirre, tha Bing a cur Hoppa-tì suas às a dèidh ach ‘s ann a tha Hoppa-tì an uairsin glacte sna geugan cuideachd! In the middle of a game, Sula’s toy hippo ends up stuck in a tree! Keen to help, Bing sends Hoppity up to rescue her but unfortunately, Hoppity also ends up caught among the branches!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing ‘S Pando a’ cluich a-muigh san fhuachd ‘s tha Flop air teòclaid theth a dhèanamh dhaibh gus an cumail blàth. Ge-tà, tha Bing a’ cur a chorragan am broinn a chupa anns a bheil an stuth goileach! Bing and Pando are playing outside, where it’s so cold they can see their breath, but Flop makes hot chocolate to warm them up. However, an impatient Bing sticks his fingers into the cup of very hot liquid!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air a bhith trang a' togail caisteal-sneachd 's iad a-nis a' coimhead air n-adhart ri geama a chluich. 'S e Hari a tha a' lorg am facal an-diugh 's e am broinn an taighe. After building a snow castle in the mountains, the Abadas settle down with Ben for the word game. Soon, Hari is sent to look for a stool inside the house.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an Cairbean-siùil a' mìneachadh mar ‘s iad na h-èisg as luaithe san fhairge agus mar ‘s ainneamh a thèid an glacadh. The Sailfish explains that they are the fastest fish in the ocean, and how they very seldom get caught by predators.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh a’ feuchainn ri bàrdachd a’ sgrìobhadh. Tha Tilidh dìreach airson fuaim a dhèanamh. ’S dòcha gun lorg iad dòigh air an dà rud a dhèanamh còmhla. Abney is trying to write poems. Teal just wants to make noise! Maybe they can find a way to do both together.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Sreath ùr anns a bheil Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann òga agus a’ faighinn a-mach ciamar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Alec agus Doris, an cat ‘Burmese’ aige. Tha Doris 8 bliadhna dh’aois agus ‘s e cat àlainn da-rìreabh a th’ innte. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh cait agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Alec agus Doris a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together, they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Alec and his beautiful Burmese cat Doris, who is eight years old. We find out about how to look after cats and all the lovely stuff Alec and Doris get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home, including how best to handle, train and feed them.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mairi NicAonghais a’ leughadh Sìle agus Dràgon. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Lesley Barnes agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Mairi MacInnes reads Sìle agus Dràgon, written and illustrated by Lesley Barnes and translated into Gaelic by Donald John Macleod.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Às deidh do Bhonns a bhith cho gionnach air Là Blàth-chnuimh’s gu bheil i air a h-uile cnuimh a bh’ann ithe, tha i a' ròghnachadh flùr blàth-chnuimh a ghoid 'o na Bògaisean gus am faigh Uilidh air blàth-chnuimh a bhlaiseadh cuideachd. When Bonns is so greedy that she eats all the grubs on Grubloom Day, she must retrieve some grubloom flowers from the Bògaisean so that Uilidh can taste a grubloom, too.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha na càraidean a' trod le chèile, tha a h-uile cail a th’ ann a’ dol bun-os-cionn aig a' Ghumbal-railidh. Ach airson fuasgladh fhaighinn, feumaidh na càraidean tighinn gu rèite airson an latha a shàbhaladh! When the twins fall out with one another, everything goes topsy turvy at the Gumbal-railidh. To solve the situation, the twins must reconcile and save the day!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha a h-uile duine a' coimhead air adhart ri oidhche shàmhach air an tuathanas nuair a tha Bitzer a' fàs an-fhoiseil - chan urrainn dha suidhe aig fois. Nuair a thòisicheas a h-uile duine eile leis an aon ghearan feumaidh Seonaidh faighinn a-mach dè tha ceàrr. Everyone is settling down for a relaxed night on the farm when Bitzer begins to act very strangely - he just can't sit still. When his peculiar behaviour starts spreading around the flock, Shaun decides he must find out what's causing it.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha e an urra ri na Pluic Fèis Bhliadhnail na Coimhearsnachd a chur air dòigh am bliadhna, ach tha na nàbaidhean farmadach aca, na h-Àrdain, a’ feuchainn ris a’ ghnothach a mhilleadh orra. It is the Spuds’ turn to run Grim Fest, the annual festival at Grimsby Heights, but their jealous neighbours, The Dups, are out to sabotage their efforts.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl sgìth de riaghailtean a mhàthar agus athar. Tha e a’ fuireach san amar ùine airson cabhag a chur air an aois, is tha seo ga thionndadh na bhodach rocach. A-nis ’s urrainn dha fhèin na riaghailtean a chruthachadh. Dave is tired of following his mum and dad’s rules. Creating a reverse fountain of youth in the bathtub, he shrivels himself into an old man and sets about making up rules of his own.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek Pluto Murray, with head judge Iain Spanish MacKay and guest judge Mairi Gillies, set some gardening-themed challenges for three couples to test their DIY skills.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Alison Lang chats to Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean experiences literature galore as he learns about a writer who made his home in Barra.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: An action-packed trip to Skye’s Trotternish peninsula with Ramsay. Cuairt thrang bheòthail gu Rubha Thròndairnis san Eilean Sgitheanach cuide ri Ramsay.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha sealg a’ ghiomaich a’ gluasad chun chladach, agus tha am mì-rian ga leantainn. Ròpaichean air an rocladh, droch nàdar a’ tighinn am bàrr, agus Steven a’ strì gus faighinn dhachaigh ann an tìde airson co-là-breith a mhic. The lobster chase moves inshore - and with it, the chaos. Tangles mount, tempers flare, and Steven races to escape the mess in time for his son’s birthday. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, writing poems, mindfulness, campervan life to playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: ’S e deagh chòcairean a th’ anns na balaich. Air prògram an latha an-diugh, tha na seòid a’ feuchainn biadh bho thaobh sear na Roinn Eòrpa. Tha Ruaraidh a’ dèanamh Feòil-tunnaig Ròsta cuide ri bonnaich bhuntàta. Tha e cuideachd a’ sealltainn mar a nithear am brot traidiseanta, Borscht. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh teanga cuide ri glasraich picilte agus Sailead Olivier, a gheibhear san Ruis. Airson deireadh gnothaich, tha e a’ dèanamh mìlsean às an Ucràin – Solozhenik Ùbhlan. The lads cook Eastern European food. Roddy makes a roast duck accompanied by potato dumplings and also demonstrates a version of the classic Borscht soup. Meanwhile Uisdean cooks a tongue to be accompanied by pickled vegetables and the classic Russian olivier salad. To finish off, he creates a Ukrainian dessert, apple solozhenik. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris le Darren Linc a chaidh a chraoladh lathaichean mus an do bhòt an Rìoghachd Aonaichte airson Brexit ann an 2016. Darren Laing’s 2016 report, first broadcast days before the United Kingdom’s vote to leave the European Union.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Julie Fowlis le taghadh ciùil bho dà dheichead den t-sreath-ciùil chliùiteach Transatlantic Sessions. Anns an 7mh prògram de Transatlantic Sessions: Dlùth an Dàimh, ceòl is òrain bho luchd-ciùil às an Rìoghachd Aonaichte, Èirinn agus na Stàitean Aonaichte. Am measg an fheadhainn a cho-obraich agus a tharraing na dùthchannan na bu dlùithe ri cheile, Aly Bain, Alison Krauss, Tim O’ Brien, Dirk Powell & Dónal Lunny. Julie Fowlis presents highlights from two decades of the legendary music show Transatlantic Sessions. This episode has musical stars from the UK, Ireland and the US, including Aly Bain, Alison Krauss, Tim O’ Brien, Dirk Powell and Dónal Lunny.

programme.title: Wainwright Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury sets off to climb her first mountain, Blencathra. Her route to the summit sees her tackle Sharp Edge, the Lake District's most technical and vertigo-inducing ridge climb. In the process, she discovers why the obsessive Wainwright chose to cover this fell in more detail than any other.

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
programme.desc: Mary Beard takes in the mythology, history and archaeology of Rome. In the first episode, Mary reaches back to the myths and legends of the origins of Rome.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s postwar exploration of Merseyside to Teesside finds him in York, a paradise for rail enthusiasts. In the company of some of the most famous locomotives ever built, he recalls the controversy surrounding their relocation from London to a freight depot in York. Michael crosses the magnificent Knaresborough viaduct, with its castellated walls and four beautiful arches over the River Nidd, to reach the spa town of Harrogate. On the edge of the elegant town, Michael discovers the gardens at Harlow Carr and learns how they opened in 1950 to test growing conditions for plants in northern climes. Across town, Michael checks into the headquarters of Yorkshire Tea. And his last destination on this leg of his journey is a bog near Skipton. In the 'gateway to the Dales', he joins members of Yorkshire Peat Partnership to find out what makes a bog.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds and Power: The Story of the Village

Presenter and archaeologist Ben Robinson discovers it wasn't just an industrial revolution. Cromford became a new kind of village, built to service the enterprise of this powerful man.

programme.title: Christopher Reeve: Keeping Hope in Motion
programme.desc: A riding accident in 1995 left Superman star Christopher Reeve paralysed and in a wheelchair. This update from 2004 to the original documentary, Hope in Motion, follows Reeve as he decides to undergo a revolutionary new operation aimed at getting him off an artificial ventilator and breathing independently again. programme.title: Ian Rankin's Hidden Edinburgh
programme.desc: Edinburgh is often described as the 'Athens of the North' but its most famous detective Inspector Rebus views Scotland's capital in quite a different light - it is a crime scene waiting to happen. As his creator Ian Rankin prepares to write the last ever Rebus case, the award-winning author re-visits the key locations from the books. From the city's 'pubic triangle' and the home of Scotland's most infamous madam to a police station where he was interviewed about a real murder, Rankin explores the hidden Edinburgh into which tourists never venture.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded asks whether the AI revolution is delivering on its promises. Companies and organisations are spending vast sums on artificial intelligence after being promised AI will transform productivity, improve efficiency and unlock entirely new ways of working. Yet a growing number of investors and analysts are asking a simple question: where's the proof? Research suggests only a small percentage of enterprise AI projects are producing measurable value. Businesses have bought the software, invested in licences and launched pilot projects, but many are still struggling to turn that investment into meaningful results. So is AI failing to live up to expectations? Or are companies simply approaching adoption the wrong way.

programme.title: The Crime I Can't Forget
programme.desc: In September 1992, Esther McCann and her 18-month-old daughter, Jessica, tragically lost their lives in a house fire in south Dublin. What seems like a tragic accident takes a more sinister turn when retired sergeant Pat Treacy and superintendent Martin Walker uncover disturbing death threats leading up to the fire, all seemingly aimed at Frank McCann, Esther's husband and a respected swimming coach. In one of the most harrowing cases of their career, Pat and Martin recall how as they dig deeper, Frank’s claims of being targeted unravel, exposing a sinister web of lies that establish him as the central focus and prime suspect in the investigation. Crime scene mapper Michael Campbell details how the truth was uncovered in the ashes of the house fire, in a case that became one of the longest running trials in Irish history. Esther McCann's niece, Esther Leonard, describes the effect these murders have had on her close-knit family and her fears for the future, if their murderer walks free.

What seems like a tragic accident takes a more sinister turn when retired sergeant Pat Treacy and superintendent Martin Walker uncover disturbing death threats leading up to the fire, all seemingly aimed at Frank McCann, Esther's husband and a respected swimming coach. In one of the most harrowing cases of their career, Pat and Martin recall how as they dig deeper, Frank’s claims of being targeted unravel, exposing a sinister web of lies that establish him as the central focus and prime suspect in the investigation. Crime scene mapper Michael Campbell details how the truth was uncovered in the ashes of the house fire, in a case that became one of the longest running trials in Irish history. Esther McCann's niece, Esther Leonard, describes the effect these murders have had on her close-knit family and her fears for the future, if their murderer walks free.

programme.title: Murder 24/7
programme.desc: When 54-year-old Jamie Gawler is found dead in his Hereford flat, DCI Gareth Lougher's team piece together his final days. But a suspect's phone yields a shocking new revelation.

programme.title: Murder 24/7
programme.desc: Phone evidence reveals the brutal extent of Matthew Jonathan's violence against Jamie Gawler. Meanwhile, the Vulnerable Persons Unit investigates a near-fatal assault in Telford.

programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A beloved wallaby mum is facing a life-threatening condition. Keepers are holding their breath as they wait to find out whether Lara is suffering from lumpy jaw, a devastating illness with no cure. If the worst happens, her young joey could be left orphaned. It’s an anxious wait as vet Alex delivers his verdict. Meanwhile, over in Lion Country, Megan and Hamza join forces for a special enrichment challenge as they find out if the big cats will hunt up trees! In the east Africa reserve, keepers are keeping a close watch on the social dynamics of the herd of roan antelope. With breeding hopes high, it’s important to weigh the females, but getting a skittish antelope onto the scales is easier said than done.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle recovery specialist Richard is on the trail of a caravan stolen during a late-night raid on a site in Nottingham. But the thieves have hidden it well, and Richard is struggling to find it before a police rural crime team send up a drone to give him a bird’s eye view of the area. Around 4,000 caravans and motorhomes are stolen every year. Nicola, from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, describes how thieves stole her caravan, not knowing it was fitted with a tracking device. A police helicopter was deployed, and the stolen van was tracked as it travelled up the M6 for about 30 miles. Eventually, it was recovered in Cheshire. Nicola is convinced that, without the tracker, she would never have seen it again. Meanwhile, tracker Joe is also in the West Midlands, closing in on a stolen Range Rover. He finds it in a workshop, where it’s in the process of being dismantled for parts. A suspect is arrested, but the car is a total write-off.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Police turn to an expert witness to help them link a drug gang to the death of a Vietnamese man in Wales. And experts in DNA and fibre analysis provide the evidence needed to convict the killer of an elderly man in Bristol.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s Roo Irvine’s turn to find out more about one of our wonderful experts and take a peek at their personal acquisition of antiques and collectibles. The teams are shopping at Oswestry Showground. The reds, barbers Max and Jake, are paired up with expert Philip Serrell. Their challenge is to buy coloured glass, while the blues, couple Atique and Laura, with expert Ben Cooper, must find an item connected to childhood. Wrexham auctioneer Matthew Tongue is on the rostrum. Will it come down to the experts' bonus buys to seal victory?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Kev's in hot water! Boiling, in fact, as he wrestles with a rusty water tank. Upholsterer Larissa needs to find a way of getting a tired set of dining chairs sitting pretty again. And Jacqui Joseph takes on her biggest challenge to date, a massive display unit, but will she manage to make it fit for a modern home?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In wonderful West Yorkshire, Nicki Chapman is with a young couple from Manchester who have a budget of £270,000 to find a home in the countryside for them and their baby son. Nicki also meets a pair who have already made their escape when they took an early retirement and swapped town life for country life on the edge of the beautiful Yorkshire Dales.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

Keepers are holding their breath as they wait to find out whether Lara is suffering from lumpy jaw, a devastating illness with no cure. If the worst happens, her young joey could be left orphaned. It’s an anxious wait as vet Alex delivers his verdict. Meanwhile, over in Lion Country, Megan and Hamza join forces for a special enrichment challenge as they find out if the big cats will hunt up trees! In the east Africa reserve, keepers are keeping a close watch on the social dynamics of the herd of roan antelope. With breeding hopes high, it’s important to weigh the females, but getting a skittish antelope onto the scales is easier said than done.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle recovery specialist Richard is on the trail of a caravan stolen during a late-night raid on a site in Nottingham. But the thieves have hidden it well, and Richard is struggling to find it before a police rural crime team send up a drone to give him a bird’s eye view of the area. Around 4,000 caravans and motorhomes are stolen every year. Nicola, from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, describes how thieves stole her caravan, not knowing it was fitted with a tracking device. A police helicopter was deployed, and the stolen van was tracked as it travelled up the M6 for about 30 miles. Eventually, it was recovered in Cheshire. Nicola is convinced that, without the tracker, she would never have seen it again. Meanwhile, tracker Joe is also in the West Midlands, closing in on a stolen Range Rover. He finds it in a workshop, where it’s in the process of being dismantled for parts. A suspect is arrested, but the car is a total write-off.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A beloved wallaby mum is facing a life-threatening condition. programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle recovery specialist Richard is on the trail of a caravan stolen during a late-night raid on a site in Nottingham. But the thieves have hidden it well, and Richard is struggling to find it before a police rural crime team send up a drone to give him a bird’s eye view of the area. Around 4,000 caravans and motorhomes are stolen every year. Nicola, from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, describes how thieves stole her caravan, not knowing it was fitted with a tracking device. A police helicopter was deployed, and the stolen van was tracked as it travelled up the M6 for about 30 miles. Eventually, it was recovered in Cheshire. Nicola is convinced that, without the tracker, she would never have seen it again. Meanwhile, tracker Joe is also in the West Midlands, closing in on a stolen Range Rover. He finds it in a workshop, where it’s in the process of being dismantled for parts. A suspect is arrested, but the car is a total write-off.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Police turn to an expert witness to help them link a drug gang to the death of a Vietnamese man in Wales. And experts in DNA and fibre analysis provide the evidence needed to convict the killer of an elderly man in Bristol.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s Roo Irvine’s turn to find out more about one of our wonderful experts and take a peek at their personal acquisition of antiques and collectibles. The teams are shopping at Oswestry Showground. The reds, barbers Max and Jake, are paired up with expert Philip Serrell. Their challenge is to buy coloured glass, while the blues, couple Atique and Laura, with expert Ben Cooper, must find an item connected to childhood. Wrexham auctioneer Matthew Tongue is on the rostrum. Will it come down to the experts' bonus buys to seal victory?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A beloved wallaby mum is facing a life-threatening condition. Keepers are holding their breath as they wait to find out whether Lara is suffering from lumpy jaw, a devastating illness with no cure. If the worst happens, her young joey could be left orphaned. It’s an anxious wait as vet Alex delivers his verdict. Meanwhile, over in Lion Country, Megan and Hamza join forces for a special enrichment challenge as they find out if the big cats will hunt up trees! In the east Africa reserve, keepers are keeping a close watch on the social dynamics of the herd of roan antelope. programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle recovery specialist Richard is on the trail of a caravan stolen during a late-night raid on a site in Nottingham. But the thieves have hidden it well, and Richard is struggling to find it before a police rural crime team send up a drone to give him a bird’s eye view of the area. Around 4,000 caravans and motorhomes are stolen every year. Nicola, from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, describes how thieves stole her caravan, not knowing it was fitted with a tracking device. A police helicopter was deployed, and the stolen van was tracked as it travelled up the M6 for about 30 miles. Eventually, it was recovered in Cheshire. Nicola is convinced that, without the tracker, she would never have seen it again. Meanwhile, tracker Joe is also in the West Midlands, closing in on a stolen Range Rover. He finds it in a workshop, where it’s in the process of being dismantled for parts. A suspect is arrested, but the car is a total write-off.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Police turn to an expert witness to help them link a drug gang to the death of a Vietnamese man in Wales. And experts in DNA and fibre analysis provide the evidence needed to convict the killer of an elderly man in Bristol.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s Roo Irvine’s turn to find out more about one of our wonderful experts and take a peek at their personal acquisition of antiques and collectibles. The teams are shopping at Oswestry Showground. The reds, barbers Max and Jake, are paired up with expert Philip Serrell. Their challenge is to buy coloured glass, while the blues, couple Atique and Laura, with expert Ben Cooper, must find an item connected to childhood. Wrexham auctioneer Matthew Tongue is on the rostrum. Will it come down to the experts' bonus buys to seal victory?

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

Keepers are holding their breath as they wait to find out whether Lara is suffering from lumpy jaw, a devastating illness with no cure. If the worst happens, her young joey could be left orphaned. It’s an anxious wait as vet Alex delivers his verdict. Meanwhile, over in Lion Country, Megan and Hamza join forces for a special enrichment challenge as they find out if the big cats will hunt up trees! In the east Africa reserve, keepers are keeping a close watch on the social dynamics of the herd of roan antelope. With breeding hopes high, it’s important to weigh the females, but getting a skittish antelope onto the scales is easier said than done.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle recovery specialist Richard is on the trail of a caravan stolen during a late-night raid on a site in Nottingham. But the thieves have hidden it well, and Richard is struggling to find it before a police rural crime team send up a drone to give him a bird’s eye view of the area. Around 4,000 caravans and motorhomes are stolen every year. Nicola, from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, describes how thieves stole her caravan, not knowing it was fitted with a tracking device. A police helicopter was deployed, and the stolen van was tracked as it travelled up the M6 for about 30 miles. Eventually, it was recovered in Cheshire. Nicola is convinced that, without the tracker, she would never have seen it again. Meanwhile, tracker Joe is also in the West Midlands, closing in on a stolen Range Rover. He finds it in a workshop, where it’s in the process of being dismantled for parts. A suspect is arrested, but the car is a total write-off.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Police turn to an expert witness to help them link a drug gang to the death of a Vietnamese man in Wales. And experts in DNA and fibre analysis provide the evidence needed to convict the killer of an elderly man in Bristol.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s Roo Irvine’s turn to find out more about one of our wonderful experts and take a peek at their personal acquisition of antiques and collectibles. The teams are shopping at Oswestry Showground. The reds, barbers Max and Jake, are paired up with expert Philip Serrell. Their challenge is to buy coloured glass, while the blues, couple Atique and Laura, with expert Ben Cooper, must find an item connected to childhood. Wrexham auctioneer Matthew Tongue is on the rostrum. Will it come down to the experts' bonus buys to seal victory?

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Hidden Lives
programme.desc: Samantha Little explores an extremely mucky pre-wedding ritual popular in the north of Scotland. Originating from an ancient custom of rubbing soot into the feet, the modern blackening is a very different affair and can be a wild and riotous occasion. The engaged couple are kidnapped and are ‘gunked’, by friends and family, who use all manner of disgusting substances, including fermented dog food, rotten eggs and even fish guts. The purpose of this revolting tradition? To bring good luck, of course! Samantha, who was blackened herself, follows two brave couples who allowed the cameras to capture every disgusting moment.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham’s beginner’s guide to vegetable growing started in April, and now it’s time to reap the rewards as he starts to harvest from the veg plot at Beechgrove Garden. Calum Clunie sows for winter crops as he starts the sowing cycle again on his family-sized plo. He also refreshes the containers he started in April as a demonstration of just what you can do if space is limited and you only room for some pots. Brian and Calum tackle Beechgrove’s hedges after checking carefully for bird nest activity, and Brian advises on caring for common houseplants. There is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden, along with the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: It’s the adventure escape category, and the Oliver family are tasked with rating the very best active getaways that Scotland has to offer. They take a trip to remote Doune Knoydart, which is only accessible by boat or a two-day hike across the mountains, Loch Ken Eco Bothies in Dumfries and Galloway, which boasts its own activity centre, and Eagle Brae, an eco-log cabin village set in an 8,000-acre estate in the heart of the Highlands. But which will they decide is worthy of a place in the grand final?

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: As the case reaches a stunning conclusion, Lindo and Bart face a race against time to find the real killer as long held secrets are finally revealed.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Spoof comedy following the first Unified Scottish Police Force. The traffic cops tackle a dodgy driver, the detectives smash a smuggling operation, and the Chief bravely faces up to encountering his ex-wife. We learn more about SPF special ops as a very important dignitary requires a level of protection that's way beyond the call of duty. And PC Jack McLaren steps in to help out using what could only be described as extreme piggy-backing.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Alan kicks off the dog benefit, while Michelle's family attends the show. Daphne shares her Icelandic plans with Alan while grappling with how to break the news to Darren.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Darren is motivated by Daphne's announcement and decides to share his ideas with Alan. Daphne, Michelle, Cunning and Jake meet up to talk about their future plans. Darren surprises Daphne with a thoughtful gift during her last performance.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: TUNE
programme.desc: Crowned Best Breakthrough Artist at this year's Radio 1 Dance Awards, Hannah Laing has earned a reputation as one of the UK’s most exciting new names in electronic music. From headlining festivals; to DJing with Idris Elba to scoring a top ten hit with her anthem Good Love, Hannah’s career - which started out in local pubs - has taken her across the globe. Raised by parents who loved to rave, Hannah grew up immersed in dance music. After seeing Dave Pearce DJ in Dundee and later meeting local promoters in the scene, Hannah landed her first gig in the small fishing town of Arbroath aged 18. From there it became her mission to DJ full-time. Despite spending summers playing in Ibiza and securing bigger slots back home, Hannah worked as a dental nurse, juggling her day job with DJing at night. Now, ten years after her first gig, Hannah prepares to make history in her hometown by becoming the first electronic DJ to headline Dundee’s iconic Caird Hall. Reflecting on how far she has come, Hannah shares the highs, lows, hard graft and determination behind her success.

Despite spending summers playing in Ibiza and securing bigger slots back home, Hannah worked as a dental nurse, juggling her day job with DJing at night. Now, ten years after her first gig, Hannah prepares to make history in her hometown by becoming the first electronic DJ to headline Dundee’s iconic Caird Hall. Reflecting on how far she has come, Hannah shares the highs, lows, hard graft and determination behind her success.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: James Arthur: Out of Our Minds
programme.desc: Multi-platinum-selling singer-songwriter James Arthur is at a crossroads in his life. After being propelled to stardom following his X Factor win in 2012, it has been a decade of highs but also desperate lows. James suffers from anxiety, depression and severe panic attacks. At his worst, he has considered taking his own life. Now 34, he is wondering if returning to the anti-depressants he has rejected might finally give him peace of mind. This documentary follows James as he explores the roots of his fragile mental health and searches for ways to cope.

programme.title: Zara McDermott
programme.desc: Record numbers of young people are being treated for eating disorders. Zara McDermott explores the reasons behind this explosion and asks if social media is part of the problem.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: It doesn't get deadlier than big game country - Steve is hot on the trail of Africa's big cats. He dons a camouflage suit to beat a leopard at its own game by hunting his crew, but it proves to be a lot harder than it looks. Nevertheless a once-in-a-lifetime experience gets him closer to a wild leopard than even he'd dare hope. After an eerie night sleeping out under the stars, Steve catches up with a pride of lions and witnesses them hunting right before his eyes, proving just how deadly lions are. Deadlier still when they start stalking him and his crew late at night!

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph is at High Wycombe recycling centre in Buckinghamshire, scouring the site for items that can be given a new lease of life rather than hitting the skips. She uncovers a vintage massage bed in need of a creative touch, but Jacqui isn't feeling zen when it comes to repurposing it. Meanwhile, upcycler Sarah Peterson tries to take a tricky dining set back in time with a brand new look.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer reaches its peak, Monty plans ahead, and after weeks of soaring temperatures, he’s got his work cut out refreshing the borders with a selection of late-summer perennials. He also has a rambling rose to tackle, and in the veg garden, the cleared beds are quickly being re-sown with crops for future harvests. Thirty years after the death of gardening legend Geoff Hamilton, Adam Frost makes a deeply personal visit to Barnsdale and reflects on the man whose huge influence helped shape both his career and love of horticulture. Carol Klein continues her fascinating journey into the secret life of plants. Exploring cutting-edge science, she discovers how vast networks of underground microbes work in partnership with plant roots, revealing the extraordinary hidden world beneath the earth. There’s an award-winning grower whose passion for gladioli has led to a collection of more than 1,800 spectacular blooms. Plus a visit to a remarkable Balinese-inspired tropical paradise nestled on the edge of the Brecon Beacons.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Sean Fletcher, Louise Minchin, Chris Washington and Kimberly Wyatt take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: As the week edges towards its conclusion, Vernon Kay brings the quiz to Jedburgh. As ever, Paul Gorton is on tour-guiding duties, delivering fun facts, fibs and distractions along the way. TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz all have their sights set on the top of the leaderboard.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: Many people regard France as the home of gastronomy and Lyon the culinary capital of France, so that is where the journey across France begins as Dave and Si explore the 'bouchon' - a restaurant traditionally run by a female chef or 'mere Lyonnaise'. As for their own efforts, they start with a tarte aux pralines and create a saucisson-stuffed brioche. After a quick stop to learn the secrets of teeth-pulling nougat in Montelimar, they go truffle-hunting for the famous white summer truffle, which they use to make truffle-infused butter and brie. En route, they also bake an apricot tarte tatin and a delectable flan de Saint Jean de Minervois (like a crème caramel but made with lavender honey and dessert wine). But it is not all baking on this trip. They also meet up with Dave's old flatmate, French Pat, who he has not seen for 30 years, and they are inducted into the Ancient Order of the Cassoulet when they reach their journey's end in Carcassonne.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: For Dartmoor tenant farmers Louise and Olly, winning prizes for their Beltex sheep at the Mid Devon Show means a lot. Louise needs that recognition as a top breeder to secure their future, which is especially important now their young children clearly love farming life. Meanwhile, Amelia and Ben are so committed to rearing their Charollais sheep that they rent land and hold down other jobs to make their farming dream pay. Show day is a chance to go head-to-head with the best breeders in the country, and for their four-year-old son to face the judge showing his own sheep.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit Toronto, as Canadians flock to the Roadshow with items from home and abroad, including an American soda siphon much sought after by country store collectors, a porcupine quill box, a valuable Newlyn School painting and fine English oak furniture. The surprise of the day is a moose-hide jacket which belonged to the leader of the historic expedition to find Sir John Franklin.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition comes from Ickworth House, a classical mansion just outside of Bury St Edmunds in Suffolk. Paul Martin is joined by experts Adam Partridge and Philip Serrell. Antiques and collectibles brought in by the public are valued by the team before being put under the hammer. Adam discusses the merits of stretchy swimsuits over a vintage bathing costume, and Philip gets a lovely surprise at the auction with an East India Company medal. Paul also visits Tate Britain in London to study the works of one of Suffolk's most famous sons - John Constable.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Gethin Jones, Tiff Stevenson, Kate Thornton and Gary Wilmot - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton guides a pair of budding entrepreneurs who want to escape to the Cotswolds. They have a generous £900,000 to play with, but the property must have the potential to develop a boutique country holiday let. Elsewhere, Alistair has an exhilarating spell at the University of Bath when he launches himself on to the UK’s only bobsleigh and skeleton push-start track.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: In the west of Britain, there's a rare medieval cemetery, a disappearing Mesolithic landscape, a mysterious Iron Age burial and the ruins of a Gothic masterpiece.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: Its April, and farmers are out, sowing the peat-based soils that make this nation’s richest source of crops, whilst also keeping an eye out for all the local wildlife.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Hard-as-nails detective inspector, divorcee and single mum Katrina is determined to crack the case of the missing boy. But there’s also her drinking, her love life and her inner demons. She doesn’t want help, but it turns up anyway.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Women Talking
programme.desc: Following a brutal realisation, the women of an isolated religious community come together to decide how they will respond. Will they forgive the men who harmed them and their children? Or withhold forgiveness and be cast out of their community, forfeiting their right to enter the Kingdom of Heaven?

programme.title: Ambulance
programme.desc: The team in ambulance control try to assist paramedics Sam and Sophie, who are deep in woodland struggling to locate a patient they’ve been told has had a fit while out on a walk.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: Many people regard France as the home of gastronomy and Lyon the culinary capital of France, so that is where the journey across France begins as Dave and Si explore the 'bouchon' - a restaurant traditionally run by a female chef or 'mere Lyonnaise'. As for their own efforts, they start with a tarte aux pralines and create a saucisson-stuffed brioche. After a quick stop to learn the secrets of teeth-pulling nougat in Montelimar, they go truffle-hunting for the famous white summer truffle, which they use to make truffle-infused butter and brie. En route, they also bake an apricot tarte tatin and a delectable flan de Saint Jean de Minervois (like a crème caramel but made with lavender honey and dessert wine). But it is not all baking on this trip. They also meet up with Dave's old flatmate, French Pat, who he has not seen for 30 years, and they are inducted into the Ancient Order of the Cassoulet when they reach their journey's end in Carcassonne.

Meanwhile, Amelia and Ben are so committed to rearing their Charollais sheep that they rent land and hold down other jobs to make their farming dream pay. Show day is a chance to go head-to-head with the best breeders in the country, and for their four-year-old son to face the judge showing his own sheep.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer reaches its peak, Monty plans ahead, and after weeks of soaring temperatures, he’s got his work cut out refreshing the borders with a selection of late-summer perennials. He also has a rambling rose to tackle, and in the veg garden, the cleared beds are quickly being re-sown with crops for future harvests. Thirty years after the death of gardening legend Geoff Hamilton, Adam Frost makes a deeply personal visit to Barnsdale and reflects on the man whose huge influence helped shape both his career and love of horticulture. Carol Klein continues her fascinating journey into the secret life of plants. Exploring cutting-edge science, she discovers how vast networks of underground microbes work in partnership with plant roots, revealing the extraordinary hidden world beneath the earth. There’s an award-winning grower whose passion for gladioli has led to a collection of more than 1,800 spectacular blooms. Plus a visit to a remarkable Balinese-inspired tropical paradise nestled on the edge of the Brecon Beacons.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Puglia meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck in producing a staple of Italian cuisine passata before discovering the history of pomegranates in this region. In an area known as 'The Tabletop' he learns how farmers work day-in day-out to produce tomatoes for passata before heading back to farmer Mario's house to help the family make their own version that will see them through the year. Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you: indulgent, delicious meatball and mozzarella ciabatta rolls. His journey then takes him South to discover an ingredient you might not associate with Italy but one that has a long heritage: pomegranates. He joins Dario as harvest begins to learn the special connection between this region and produce. After a hard day's work Tom cooks lamb cutlets with pomegranate couscous to celebrate.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip; Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Paris to take on The Vixen and The Beast, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on an open top bus around the Arc de Triomphe. The race across the city forces the teams to navigate their way to the finish line by successfully completing games involving waxworks, snails, Notre Dame, and a captive music quiz in the back of a taxi!

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Puglia meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck in producing a staple of Italian cuisine passata before discovering the history of pomegranates in this region. In an area known as 'The Tabletop' he learns how farmers work day-in day-out to produce tomatoes for passata before heading back to farmer Mario's house to help the family make their own version that will see them through the year. Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you: indulgent, delicious meatball and mozzarella ciabatta rolls. His journey then takes him South to discover an ingredient you might not associate with Italy but one that has a long heritage: pomegranates. He joins Dario as harvest begins to learn the special connection between this region and produce. After a hard day's work Tom cooks lamb cutlets with pomegranate couscous to celebrate.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip; Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Paris to take on The Vixen and The Beast, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on an open top bus around the Arc de Triomphe. The race across the city forces the teams to navigate their way to the finish line by successfully completing games involving waxworks, snails, Notre Dame, and a captive music quiz in the back of a taxi!

programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Puglia meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In an area known as 'The Tabletop' he learns how farmers work day-in day-out to produce tomatoes for passata before heading back to farmer Mario's house to help the family make their own version that will see them through the year. Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you: indulgent, delicious meatball and mozzarella ciabatta rolls. His journey then takes him South to discover an ingredient you might not associate with Italy but one that has a long heritage: pomegranates. programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Puglia meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck in producing a staple of Italian cuisine passata before discovering the history of pomegranates in this region. In an area known as 'The Tabletop' he learns how farmers work day-in day-out to produce tomatoes for passata before heading back to farmer Mario's house to help the family make their own version that will see them through the year. Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you: indulgent, delicious meatball and mozzarella ciabatta rolls. His journey then takes him South to discover an ingredient you might not associate with Italy but one that has a long heritage: pomegranates. He joins Dario as harvest begins to learn the special connection between this region and produce. After a hard day's work Tom cooks lamb cutlets with pomegranate couscous to celebrate.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip; Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Paris to take on The Vixen and The Beast, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on an open top bus around the Arc de Triomphe. The race across the city forces the teams to navigate their way to the finish line by successfully completing games involving waxworks, snails, Notre Dame, and a captive music quiz in the back of a taxi!

In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck in producing a staple of Italian cuisine passata before discovering the history of pomegranates in this region. In an area known as 'The Tabletop' he learns how farmers work day-in day-out to produce tomatoes for passata before heading back to farmer Mario's house to help the family make their own version that will see them through the year. Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you: indulgent, delicious meatball and mozzarella ciabatta rolls. His journey then takes him South to discover an ingredient you might not associate with Italy but one that has a long heritage: pomegranates. He joins Dario as harvest begins to learn the special connection between this region and produce. After a hard day's work Tom cooks lamb cutlets with pomegranate couscous to celebrate.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip; Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Paris to take on The Vixen and The Beast, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on an open top bus around the Arc de Triomphe. The race across the city forces the teams to navigate their way to the finish line by successfully completing games involving waxworks, snails, Notre Dame, and a captive music quiz in the back of a taxi!
